patch_description: Add a fifth candidate construction: a conditional prefix partition tree. Within each group of rows, pick the remaining column with the largest length-weighted pair repetition sum(len(v)*cnt*(cnt-1)) using precomputed integer factorizations and vectorized bincount, place it at the front, partition rows by its factorized value code, and recurse on the suffix separately per group. This produces per-row column orderings (explicitly allowed by the API), which lets rows with different shared leading values get different optimized orders — something no global ordering can achieve. Guard: only run when col_merge is empty, scoring is enabled, total chars <= 30M, and depth is bounded (12 when n_cols>=8 and n_rows<=200k, else 8), with at most 10 split candidates per node. Score the tree with the exact sorted-adjacent LCP Trie objective and select it only if it actually beats all global orderings. Output applies each row's permutation to that row's values (object dtype, all cells preserved) with matching per-row column_orderings. This targets the weaker datasets (0.44/0.62 hit rates) where row-conditional structure exists but global orders cannot exploit it, while the exact-objective selection prevents regressions.
